titleEn: The Secret of a Shorter Subway Transfer
lead: 讲大城市地铁换乘靠颜色、标识、箭头和电梯的“智能设计”让人少走冤枉路、坐对方向。全文 23 句、5 段，实用说明文，句间逻辑靠 first / next / during / before 串起来，适合练“按顺序找信息”。原卷未给答案，本页答案为依据原文推断，仅供参考。
paragraphs: In many big cities, the subway is the fastest way to travel. However, changing lines can be confusing for new riders. Today, city planners use smart design to help people find their way easily.

When you enter a busy interchange station, look at the colors first. Each subway line has its own special color on the walls and maps. This clear signage helps you tell different lines apart quickly. Following the right color saves you time before you even walk far.

Next, you need to find the correct platform for your train. Do not just look at the platform number alone. You must check both the number and the direction together carefully. Trains on the same platform often go in opposite directions. Good navigation means reading every detail on the boards above you. Arrows will point you to the right path safely.

During a transfer, always follow the colored arrows on the floor or walls. They guide you step by step to the next line without wrong turns. But remember, the shortest stairs are not always the best choice for everyone. If you push a wheelchair or a baby car, stairs are hard to use. Modern stations focus heavily on accessibility for all kinds of passengers. People with special needs might have to take a longer but smoother route. Elevators are usually placed along these specific accessible paths.

Before you leave the transfer hall, stop to check your route one last time. Make sure the line color matches your final destination again. Smart design makes our daily travel much easier and friendlier than before.

questions.q: What should you look at first when you enter a busy interchange station?
questions.qZh: 走进繁忙的换乘站时，你应该先看什么？

options.t: The platform numbers
options.tZh: 站台号

options.t: Colors on the walls and maps
options.tZh: 墙面和地图上的颜色

options.t: The arrows on the floor
options.tZh: 地面上的箭头

options.t: The elevators in the hall
options.tZh: 大厅里的电梯

questions.evidence: When you enter a busy interchange station, look at the colors first.
questions.evidenceZh: 细节题：第二段第一句就用 look at the colors first 直接给了顺序，first 是关键词。

questions.q: Why might some people take a longer route during a transfer?
questions.qZh: 换乘时，为什么有些人会走一条更长的路线？

options.t: Because they want to see more of the station
options.tZh: 因为他们想多看看车站

options.t: Because the shorter stairs are closed for repair
options.tZh: 因为较短的楼梯在维修、封了

options.t: Because they need to use elevators instead of stairs
options.tZh: 因为他们需要坐电梯代替走楼梯

options.t: Because they like walking slowly with friends
options.tZh: 因为他们喜欢和朋友慢慢走

questions.evidence: If you push a wheelchair or a baby car, stairs are hard to use. … People with special needs might have to take a longer but smoother route. Elevators are usually placed along these specific accessible paths.
questions.evidenceZh: 因果题：楼梯用不了（stairs are hard to use）→ 走更长更平顺的路（longer but smoother route）→ 因为要坐电梯（elevators）。

questions.q: How can you make sure you get on the right train?
questions.qZh: 怎样才能确保坐上正确的列车？

options.t: Only read the platform number quickly
options.tZh: 只快速看一眼站台号

options.t: Ask other passengers which way to go
options.tZh: 问其他乘客往哪走

options.t: Take the shortest stairs you can find
options.tZh: 走你能找到的最短的楼梯

options.t: Check the color and direction, and follow the arrows to the right platform
options.tZh: 核对颜色和方向，跟着箭头走到正确的站台

questions.evidence: You must check both the number and the direction together carefully. … Arrows will point you to the right path safely.
questions.evidenceZh: 细节题：第三段给出两件事——number 与 direction 一起核对，再跟着 arrows 走。选项 A 正是原文否定的做法（Do not just look at the platform number alone）。

questions.q: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.qZh: 这篇文章的主旨是什么？

options.t: Subway trains are faster than buses in big cities
options.tZh: 在大城市，地铁比公交快

options.t: How smart design helps passengers change subway lines easily
options.tZh: 智能设计如何帮助乘客轻松换乘地铁

options.t: Why new riders should not take the subway alone
options.tZh: 为什么新乘客不该独自坐地铁

options.t: Where to find elevators in a modern subway station
options.tZh: 在现代地铁站里哪里能找到电梯

questions.evidence: Today, city planners use smart design to help people find their way easily. … Smart design makes our daily travel much easier and friendlier than before.
questions.evidenceZh: 主旨题：首段的 smart design + help people find their way 与末段的 smart design + easier 首尾呼应；A、C、D 都只是文中一句话的局部信息。

questions.q: In the last paragraph, what does the word 'destination' mean?
questions.qZh: 最后一段中 destination 一词是什么意思？

options.t: The ticket you buy at the station
options.tZh: 你在车站买的票

options.t: The train you wait for on the platform
options.tZh: 你在站台等的列车

options.t: The place you want to go to
options.tZh: 你要去的地方

options.t: The time your train leaves
options.tZh: 列车开出的时间

questions.evidence: Before you leave the transfer hall, stop to check your route one last time. Make sure the line color matches your final destination again.
questions.evidenceZh: 猜词题：destination 与 route（路线）搭配，指“要去的终点”；de- 表指向、-ation 是名词后缀，字面就是“被指定的地方”。
